title: Separate Rings of Latitude on a Sphere
full_prompt: Write a ManimGL script that visualizes a sphere sliced into horizontal rings of latitude. First, render a blue sphere and fade in 50 horizontal rings of latitude stacked along the z-axis, with their radii matching the sphere's profile. Reorient the camera to a 3D perspective. Highlight the middle ring (equator) in yellow while dimming the other rings. Finally, use a ValueTracker to animate this highlighted ring sliding up and down the sphere along the z-axis, dynamically updating its radius to match the sphere's curvature ($r = \sqrt{1 - z^2}$).

common_failure_modes.pattern: Using 2D circles instead of 3D circles oriented along the OUT/Z axis
common_failure_modes.note: Circles must be positioned along the Z-axis (z * OUT) to correctly slice the 3D sphere.

common_failure_modes.pattern: Incorrect radius formula for latitude rings
common_failure_modes.note: The radius of a ring at height z must be math.sqrt(1 - z**2) to lie on the unit sphere.

common_failure_modes.pattern: Missing or incorrect updater for sliding ring
common_failure_modes.note: The sliding ring must dynamically update both its width/radius and its Z-position based on the ValueTracker.
